title: Model routing overlay
description: One layer above the catalog. Every field is optional: an overlay changes what it names and leaves the rest of the layer below it untouched. The host names the layers and their order (src/host.ts routingPaths).

note.description: Free text for whoever opens the file next. The mechanism never reads it.

weights.description: Strategy weights in percent. A named strategy is replaced whole, not merged field by field: a half-replaced weight set would silently stop summing to 100.

unknownAvailability.description: Points subtracted from a candidate whose availability is unknown, on top of counting its remaining limit as a neutral 50 per cent.

liveParticipantPerHarness.description: Points subtracted per participant already live on that harness.

liveParticipantCap.description: Ceiling for the sum of the above. Without it a busy harness would be unreachable rather than expensive.

reviewerDiversity.description: Points added to a reviewer candidate whose harness or model differs from the worker's.

reviewerQualityFloor.description: ALIAS for qualityFloor.reviewer, kept so an overlay written for v1 keeps its meaning (ADR-004). A layer stating both is a models validate warning and the explicit key wins.

qualityFloor.description: Lowest quality rating a candidate of that role should have. Defaults: worker 3, reviewer 5 (ADR-004, superseding ADR-003's reviewer floor of 4 and its absence of a worker floor). A soft floor and a CHOICE RULE, not a filter: a candidate below it keeps its place and its score, only the pick moves past it, and when nothing reaches it the best remaining candidate is chosen with a warning.

balance.description: The two numbers of the balance strategy's pace layer, both in PERCENTAGE POINTS of a window — the unit usedPercent is already in — and both defaulting to 5.

band.description: Harnesses within this many points of the leader's effective underspend are tied, and the balanced score of their representatives decides. Its job is not to model noise, but the noise floor is about a point — one harness reports usedPercent as an integer, and a sixty-second cache entry moves a five-hour window by a third of a point — so a band below that would do nothing.

spendUnit.description: The discount a heavy tuple gives up before harnesses are compared: spendUnit × (quotaCost − 1) / 4. Equal to the band by default, so a quotaCost of 5 gives up exactly one band against a quotaCost of 1 — the heaviest tuple has to be a whole band ahead on pace to win.

nearLimit.description: When models says an account is running short (ADR-004). Two readings of the same binding window, and either one on its own raises the line.

usedPercent.description: A LEVEL: how much of the binding window is gone. Default 80.

underspend.description: A RATE, in percentage points of the window: how far the account is AHEAD of its own pace. Default -15 — fifteen points more of the window spent than has elapsed of it. Negative on purpose and unbounded below; a positive value would fire on every harness that is behind pace, which is every harness the balance strategy is happy about.

defaults.description: What a command uses when the flag is absent. The one key models strategy --set writes, into the host's writable layer. Merged as a scalar: the highest layer that names one wins.

strategy.description: The strategy spawn and review route with when --strategy is absent. A flag a person typed always wins. With no default anywhere the legacy path is unchanged — a call with no --strategy routes nothing. `auto` is not a value: it is a skill decision.

account.description: A person's answers to questions no harness method returns — today one, Cursor's plan name. NOTHING WRITES THIS: models prints the key, the value and the path of the layer, and a person or an agent adds the line (ADR-004). The value is display only and enters no score; the snapshot keeps what was measured, and this is printed beside it as the person's answer.

allow.description: Allow-lists. A non-empty list means: only these. An empty list is a shape error, not 'allow nothing' — write a deny rule for that. Allow lists INTERSECT across layers: a tuple must be named by every allow list of that kind any layer states, so a layer's rule survives every layer above it. Two layers can therefore intersect to nothing, which models validate reports as allow-intersection-empty.

deny.description: Deny-lists, applied after allow. Deny lists ACCUMULATE across layers: a ban written in any layer stands and no layer above it lifts one — lifting a ban means changing the layer that wrote it. A name allowed in one layer and denied in another is lawful and deny wins, which models validate reports as the allow-shadowed-by-deny warning; a name both allowed and denied in ONE layer stays an error.

ratings.description: Rating overrides by tuple id. Only the named ratings are replaced.

priority.description: Canonical-priority overrides by tuple id. Lower comes first.

allow.description: Whether pay-as-you-go tuples take part in automatic selection without the --allow-payg flag.

weight.description: Percent. The four of a set sum to 100; the sum is checked by models validate, not by this schema.

byRole.description: The same rule block, scoped to one role. A role is a condition on when a rule applies rather than a thing that can be banned, so it nests instead of standing beside the selectors above. When routing role R the effective deny of a kind is the unscoped list unioned with byRole.R's, and the effective allow is the intersection of the two where both are stated.

roleSelectors.description: Selectors inside a byRole block. The same four names and flags; byRole does not nest inside itself — a rule is scoped to one role or to none.

flagList.description: Marks the availability snapshot carries on a model row. The one selector whose names are in no catalog — a flag is not a catalog fact — so they are checked against this closed list, which is the snapshot schema's own flags enum. A new mark a harness starts printing needs a release rather than a data change; the price of catching a person's typo. MODEL_FLAGS in lib/model-routing/catalog.js is the same list and the suite reads the two as one.
